A1.justification: Despite the changed title and journal formatting, both PDFs describe the same Marvel framework and retain matching experiments. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments, Q-value correlation measurements, baseline comparisons, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original experimental results and adds evaluated baselines, including CDT finetuning and behavior-policy Q-value distillation.

M1.justification: The VPA objectives and overall training framework remain intact, but the reported aPID equations change: v1 adds PID contributions to the previous multiplier and uses tanh in proportional-gain adaptation; v3 specifies a clipped position-form multiplier and removes tanh. V3 describes its detailed controller formulation as matching the implementation, so these documented revisions do not establish that the underlying code changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten Bullet Safety Gym/Safety Gymnasium environments and DSRL data supplemented with random-policy data. The added comparisons reuse existing environments; no new dataset, population, or environmental test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: V3 adds evaluated Cal-QL and SAC-lag with an offline replay buffer comparisons in Figure 6, CDT/CDT-finetune in Table 5, and BC-distilled critics in Figure 15. Table 2 also includes From Scratch in the BEAR-lag comparisons, where v1's Figure 4 omitted it. These substantially broaden the comparison methods beyond the retained original baselines.

E3.justification: New comparison settings include a roughly 600k-parameter CDT updated online using a replay buffer and a behavior-cloning-then-off-policy-evaluation procedure for critic initialization. The retained experiments preserve their reported cost thresholds, episode horizons, network sizes, learning rates, and interaction/update convention.

E4.justification: V3 adds a diagnostic comparing critics distilled from a cloned behavior policy with Marvel's initialization, while removing v1's unconstrained-RL check from Appendix D.8 and Figure 15. The existing critic, entropy, initialization, data-quality, parameter-sensitivity, and FSRL implementation analyses remain; their relocation and new tabular summaries are not new ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging experiments over five random seeds and using ten Monte Carlo simulations for reference Q-values. Both show variation bands, without a newly introduced empirical uncertainty definition, confidence interval, significance test, or repeated-run reporting practice.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial results for the new baselines and exact early-checkpoint and ablation entries. Most retained endpoints are equivalent after rounding, but Marvel's reported HalfCheetah reward/cost changes from 1543.17/20.31 in v1 Table 2 to 1544.8/20.0 in v3 Table 2. V1's unconstrained results and exact endpoint table for four supplementary environments disappear, although those environments' learning curves remain.

T1.justification: V1 contains no corresponding convergence analysis. V3 introduces Theorem 1's VPA estimation-error bound and Appendix H's concentrability assumption, entropy-regularized Bellman operator, contraction theorem, bounded-value lemma, and proof separating approximation and iteration errors. This is a substantial new theoretical component.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first policy-finetuning framework for offline-to-online safe RL, identify erroneous Q-estimates and multiplier mismatch, propose VPA plus aPID, and claim rapid safe learning with compatibility across existing algorithms. The revised title, wording, and additional supporting evidence do not materially redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds an explanation of residual OOD overoptimism through imperfect coverage and function approximation, and attributes BC-distillation safety failures to unsafe behavior inherited from the data. It also discusses resetting the non-decreasing derivative gain under non-stationarity. The earlier AntRun limitation is retained.

D1.justification: V3 expands Algorithm 1 and documents controller smoothing, derivative buffering, integral clipping, and gain bounds of 0.1 to 10 times their initial values. It also discloses use of a single Nvidia 4080 GPU. The main hyperparameter and environment-configuration tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Most related-work discussion is retained. V3 adds positioning relative to Luo et al.'s critic reconstruction and Zhou et al.'s offline-data-free finetuning, plus Agarwal et al. as theoretical support, while removing the Sutton and PID textbook references. Cal-QL and CDT were already cited in v1; their new evaluations are distinct from citation additions.

P1.justification: V3 substantially rewrites the abstract, contribution paragraph, PID exposition, and experimental narrative. It reorganizes the ablation discussion, introduces dedicated appendix subsections, and changes how the main results are presented and explained. These revisions extend beyond the title, affiliation, and citation-style edits.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a journal layout, moves and shrinks benchmark plots into the appendix, replaces the BEAR-lag learning-curve display with table entries, and introduces redesigned numerical summaries and new baseline displays. Tables add checkpoint columns and safety-based highlighting; the former unconstrained-RL figure is removed.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's narrower comparisons and schematic PID description, v3 provides useful additional baselines, clearer numerical summaries, and a more explicit controller specification. These improve scrutiny and reproducibility. However, Appendix H gives inconsistent approximation-error formulas, and Figure 15 incorrectly describes the BC baseline's higher but unsafe rewards as lower returns. These problems limit the overall benefit of the added theory and analysis.
